faqs.question: Why do I need color ink cartridges when I print in black only?
faqs.answer:
The printer will not print if any ink cartridge is expended or removed. Epson printers contain a permanent print head that needs to be charged with all colors to work. Even when you are printing black text only, a small amount of color ink is used to keep the print head charged. The print head needs to be kept charged to prevent air bubbles from entering. Air bubbles can damage the print head.
Therefore, once one of the cartridges is expended, the printer signals you to replace the cartridge in order for printing to continue.

faqs.question: I see the message Ink Cartridge Error: Replace Ink Cartridge. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
An ink cartridge in your printer needs to be replaced. The cartridge may be expended, or the IC chip on the cartridge may not be communicating properly. Try reseating the cartridge and turning the printer off and on. If you still see the error message, try installing a different ink cartridge in the printer.
If this did not solve the problem, contact Epson support.

faqs.question: Can I use an expired ink cartridge in my printer?
faqs.answer:
Epson does not recommend using expired ink cartridges in the printer. Do not use an unopened ink cartridge if the date on the package has expired. For best results, use ink cartridges before the expiration date printed on the package (and within six months of installation in the printer). Replace expired cartridges with new ones.
You may need to replace a cartridge that is more than six months old, if your printouts do not look their best, even after cleaning and aligning the printhead. We recommend you store any unused or unopened ink cartridges in a cool, dark place.

faqs.question: How does Epson UltraChrome K3 with Vivid Magenta reduce metamerism?
faqs.answer: By using new pigments, resin encapsulation, three levels of black, and a new screening algorithm, we've been able to reduce the effects of metamerism and bronzing from both color and black and white prints to a level below what the human eye can detect.

faqs.question: Do the Epson UltraChrome K3 with Vivid Magenta inks have less outgassing than the Epson UltraChrome Inks?
faqs.answer:
The new Epson UltraChrome K3 with Vivid Magenta inks have about the same outgassing as the previous ink set. So, depending upon the environmental conditions, Epson recommends that you let your prints outgas into interleaving papers (Epson Singleweight Matte, Doubleweight Matte, and Presentation Matte all make great interleaving papers) for at least 48 hours before framing.
Note
: You must replace the interleaving paper after 24 hours with a fresh sheet. Be sure to frame the print properly, so that the glass or UV acrylic does not touch the print.

faqs.question: Does my product have a pressurized ink delivery system?
faqs.answer: Yes. This ensures positive ink flow even when the printer is used at higher elevations or if the floor is not completely level.

faqs.question: Do the 700ml ink cartridges stick out of the front of my product?
faqs.answer: No. The 700ml ink cartridges do not extend out of the ink bay, so the ink bay door can remain closed.

faqs.question: How does Epson UltraChrome K3 with Vivid Magenta Ink achieve such a wide color gamut?
faqs.answer: Epson UltraChrome K3 ink uses higher-density pigments along with a higher-gloss resin encapsulation to produce prints with an extremely wide color gamut. Now enhanced with our revolutionary new Vivid Magenta pigments, our newest-generation ink technology is capable of producing (for most prints) a color gamut that is better than virtually any dye-based printer.

faqs.question: How does Epson UltraChrome K3 with Vivid Magenta reduce gloss differential?
faqs.answer: Gloss differential is reduced by higher gloss resin encapsulation technology and the three-level black system. UltraChrome K3 dramatically reduces the effects of gloss differential from both color and black and white prints on even the glossiest media, such as Epson Premium Glossy Photo Paper, without a gloss optimizer.

faqs.answer: There are too many variables to provide a count. You can estimate the amount by printing a Job Information sheet from the printer's Test Print menu. This sheet provides the amount of ink used for the last 10 print jobs, which can help you calculate ink usage.

faqs.question: My printer's ink cartridges are half full after I install the first set of ink cartridges. Why does this happen?
faqs.answer: Ink from the first set of ink cartridges is used to charge the printer's ink delivery system. This will not happen again when you install new ink cartridges.

faqs.question: Can I use an expired ink cartridge in my printer?
faqs.answer:
Epson does not recommend using expired ink cartridges in the printer. Do not use an unopened ink cartridge if the date on the package has expired. For best results, use ink cartridges before the expiration date printed on the package (and within six months of installation in the printer). Replace expired cartridges with new ones.
You may need to replace a cartridge that is more than six months old, if your printouts do not look their best, even after cleaning and aligning the printhead. We recommend you store any unused or unopened ink cartridges in a cool, dark place.

faqs.question: I can tell some ink is still in the ink cartridge. Why does my printer show that the cartridge is expended?
faqs.answer: The ink cartridge is designed to include a small safety reserve of ink. This safety reserve prevents damage to the printhead. If the printer tries to print when no ink remains in the cartridge, air bubbles would enter the ink delivery system and cause damage to the permanent printhead. The safety reserve of ink prevents this from happening.

faqs.answer: Your RIP software has the cut setting enabled within the paper profile, which overrides the Auto Cut off setting on the printer. Please contact your RIP software support for instructions on disabling the cutter option in the paper profile.

faqs.question: Why are Epson UltraChrome K3 with Vivid Magenta ink prints so scratch-resistant? And what about fine art papers?
faqs.answer:
Epson UltraChrome K3 Ink Technology uses a different method of “binding” the particle of pigment and the glossy resin encapsulation called “Crosslinking Chemistry.” This chemical process makes the prints harder than the previous Epson UltraChrome Ink technology, significantly increasing the scratch resistance on normal RC or Photographic-grade media types.
Fine art papers also benefit. However, although the ink is harder to scratch off, the surface of the print can get “scuffed” and the print may appear to have a “scratch” (Similar to moving your hand across a suede jacket). The ink may not come off, but you can still ruin the print. So be careful when handling prints on this media.

faqs.question: Which Epson media types produce the highest Dmax or L* value?
faqs.answer: Testing has shown that using Photo Black ink on Epson Premium Luster Photo Paper will produce a Dmax up to 2.4 with an L* value as low as 3.1. You may get different results depending upon the media, black ink mode, driver settings, and ICC profile used.

faqs.question: When I try to print a media tracking bar code on roll paper, my product ejects the paper out the paper feed path and then prints the barcode on my product's platen. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
This problem occurs when the printer's Automatic Media Tracking System is turned on and the Auto Cut feature is turned off. When the paper is cut manually, the printer can't detect the top of form position after the paper is cut, so when it feeds the paper back in, the printer feeds it too far and prints on the platen instead of the paper.
To prevent the paper from being fed too far after you cut the paper manually, push the
up arrow button on the control panel until the top edge of the paper rolls up to the arrow above the scissors image. Then you can continue printing.

Use ICC profiles during the color management process.

faqs.question: What is the Epson Advanced Black & White Printing Mode?
faqs.answer: This is a proprietary Epson screening and color management technology designed specifically to produce professional-level black and white prints. This unique screen technology takes advantage of our three-level black technology—along with Yellow, Light Cyan, and Light Magenta—to produce professional black and white prints from either color or grayscale files. Epson's new Advanced Black and White printing technology is simply another tool for achieving the ultimate black and white print.

faqs.question: What does the Common Updater 7.0 file do?
faqs.answer: The Common Updater 7.0 file provides the latest Mac OS X 10.6 support for your printer driver. Before installing the updater, make sure the most current version of the Mac OS X 10.5 or 10.6 printer driver is installed on your computer. Restart your computer after installing the updater.

faqs.question: What does the Media Bar-Code Tracking and Identification System do?
faqs.answer: The automatic media barcode tracking and identification system will keep track of what media is loaded and the amount remaining on the roll. When a partially consumed roll is removed, the printer will automatically print a small barcode on the edge of the paper that will identify the paper when it is reinserted.

faqs.question: Do I need a raster image processor (RIP) to print from Adobe Illustrator?
faqs.answer:
For the best output, a RIP should be used. Adobe Illustrator is a postscript application that requires a RIP to translate the postscript language. The printer comes with a non-postscript driver that has difficulty translating the postscript language.
Epson has partnered with the following manufacturers for some printers:

efi
Onyx
Wasatch

faqs.question: I can't get Epson Status Monitor to work over my wireless network. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
If the product is not shared, make sure it is connected to the network wirelessly. Try moving your product or computer to a different location within range of your wireless network. Avoid placing the computer, product, or wireless access point near microwaves, cordless telephones, or other sources of wireless interference.
If the product is set up as a shared printer, Epson Status Monitor will not work and is not supported.

faqs.question: How do I replace a maintenance tank?
faqs.answer:
Follow these steps to replace the tank:
Check the printer's LCD to determine which tank needs to be replaced.
Unpack the new maintenance tank and save the plastic bag it came in.
Grasp the handle at the bottom of the maintenance tank in the printer that needs to be replaced, and gently pull it straight out of the printer.
Caution
: Be careful not to spill ink from the maintenance tank when removing it. Hold it upright at all times.
Place the used tank in the plastic bag included with the new tank, and dispose of it properly.
Insert the new tank all the way into its compartment.

faqs.answer: You can purchase the optional Retractable Fabric Media Bin (Part number C12C890401) from your local dealer.

faqs.answer: The serial number is located on a tag below the bar code label on the back of the printer.

faqs.question: What is the widest roll media that I can use on my product?
faqs.answer: You can use rolls up to 64” wide.

faqs.question: What is the minimum and maximum supported paper width I can use with my product?
faqs.answer:
If you are using roll media the minimum width is 16” (406 mm) and the maximum is 64” (1626 mm).
If you are using cut sheet media the minimum width is 8.25” (210 mm) and the maximum is 64” (1626 mm).

faqs.question: Is an extended warranty available for my product?
faqs.answer: Yes, there are two plans available. A One-Year extended warranty (part# EPP1188B1, MSRP $1495.00) and a Two-Year extended warranty (part# EPP1188B2, MSRP $2695.00).

faqs.answer: It includes one Hi-speed USB 2.0 (1.1 compatible) and one Gigabit Ethernet Port (10/100/1000Base-T).

Pause

is highlighted.

On
.
Turn the printer off then back on.
Note:
Sylon Mode works only when the printer is printing.  If the printer is idle, ready, or in an error state, the ink status lights do not strobe.
